texts: good. the full-moon state is recorded with the moon as the one it holds of, dated with both Year 1 and day 47, and the plain past "the moon was full" is kept alongside it. One caveat for the corpus rather than for this sentence: day 47 goes into the same slot an ordinary day-of-the-month would use, so keep every episode's dateline in exactly this "day N of Year M" wording or dates from different episodes will not line up.

mixed: the convening itself is right — the Council as the one convening, the Watch as the place, past tense, and this is the Council symbol every later sentence reuses — but nothing carries the episode's dateline onto it, so "when did the Council convene?" finds nothing; the translator never borrows a date from a neighbouring sentence. If the session is meant to fall on that date, write: "That day, the Council convened at the Watch." — an explicit "that day" copies day 47 and Year 1 onto the convening. The same holds for every later event in the episode: each is dated only if its own sentence says so.

mixed: the report is sealed the right way — Sailsworn reporting, the Council as addressee, and nothing about the store's stock asserted as fact — but "fourteen weeks of winter supply" has no licensed form: an amount stated as how long it lasts ends up as a duration measured on the supply itself, which is the slot for how long an event lasts. Rewrite as: "Sailsworn reported to the Council that the salt-bloom store held winter supply that would last fourteen weeks." — the fourteen weeks then measure a lasting, which is what that slot is for, and the store, the holding and the winter supply are otherwise unchanged.

mixed: everything stated lands (the Council issues, the ration is marked standard, the Stilllight Station is a named station receiving it), but "winter feather ration" fuses into a single kind linked upward only to "ration" — it is not linked to the plain "feather ration" of the last two sentences, so a question about feather rations will not find this one. Rewrite as: "The Council issued the standard feather ration for winter to the Stilllight Station." — that keeps "winter" as a stated qualifier while putting the ration in the same feather-ration kind the rest of the episode uses.

good. the report seals correctly and "had remained free of wraiths" comes through as a continuing free-of-wraiths state of the named Lantern, with the past perfect kept inside the report and nothing about the Lantern asserted as fact outside it.

mixed: same problem as Sailsworn's report — the reporting structure is right, but "eight weeks of supply" makes the eight weeks a duration measured on the supply itself, the slot for how long an event lasts rather than for how much stock is on hand. Rewrite as: "Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the feather store held supply that would last eight weeks."

good. a second, separate issuing event to the same Stilllight Station with its own extra ration, correctly kept distinct from the standard ration issued earlier. Note only that nothing connects this issuance to Tessa Brae's report — sentences placed side by side record no relation between them, so if the extra ration is a response to the eight-week figure, that has to be said in words.

bad: "the stations of the West Row" becomes one group standing as a single recipient, so the parse says one extra ration went to those stations taken together; if each station got its own extra ration that reading is lost and "did station X get an extra ration?" will not resolve — the per-member machinery fires on a plural subject, never on a recipient. Rewrite as: "Each station of the West Row received an extra feather ration from the Council." — an explicit "each" in subject position is what triggers the per-station reading, and the Council stays the issuer. If one pooled ration for the whole Row is what you meant, say that instead: "The Council issued a single extra feather ration to the West Row as a whole."
